content:
Unveiled alongside the new Mac mini, Apple today launched the next-generation Mac Studio. The new Mac Studio lineup features the M5 Max and M5 Ultra chips, supporting up to 512GB of unified memory.

The new Mac Studio models are available for pre-order starting today.

M5 Max Mac Studio

First, Apple announced the new Mac Studio powered by the M5 Max, an upgrade over last year's M4 Max model. The M5 Max first debuted earlier this year in the MacBook Pro.

The M5 Max features an 18-core CPU, including 6 performance cores and 12 efficiency cores. The GPU can be configured with up to 40 cores, with each core featuring a built-in Neural Engine accelerator. Apple says GPU performance is up to 50% faster than the previous generation. Unified memory bandwidth reaches up to 614GB/s, an improvement over the 546GB/s of the M4 Max generation.

The M5 Max Mac Studio comes standard with 36GB of unified memory, configurable up to 128GB. For comparison, the M4 Max Mac Studio launched with the same specifications. However, over the past year, due to industry-wide memory shortages, Apple has gradually reduced available configurations. As of yesterday, the M4 Max Mac Studio's memory options started at 36GB and topped out at 96GB.

Below are some benchmark figures for the M5 Max Mac Studio shared by Apple:

  • LLM prompt processing speed in LM Studio is up to 10.7x faster than the Mac Studio with M1 Max, and up to 3.9x faster than M4 Max.
  • Text-to-image performance is up to 7.4x faster than the Mac Studio with M1 Max, and up to 3.5x faster than M4 Max.
  • Magic Mask performance in Blackmagic Design DaVinci Resolve Studio is up to 5.3x faster than the Mac Studio with M1 Max, and up to 3x faster than M4 Max.
  • DNA sequencing basecalling speed in Oxford Nanopore MinKNOW is up to 3.5x faster than the Mac Studio with M1 Max, and up to 1.9x faster than M4 Max.

M5 Ultra Mac Studio

The real star of today's announcement is the M5 Ultra Mac Studio.

The new M5 Ultra Mac Studio features up to a 36-core CPU, including 12 performance cores and 24 efficiency cores, delivering up to 1.3x faster multithreaded performance compared to the previous-generation M3 Ultra Mac Studio.

The M5 Ultra incorporates up to an 80-core GPU, which Apple describes as the most powerful GPU ever built into Apple silicon. This is also the first time Apple has added Neural Engine accelerators to an Ultra chip. The Neural Engine accelerator is dedicated hardware built into each GPU core, specifically designed to accelerate AI workloads.

In terms of memory, the Mac Studio with M5 Ultra starts at 96GB and can be configured up to 512GB—the same as when the M3 Ultra Mac Studio originally launched. However, over the past year, due to memory shortages, Apple reduced the M3 Ultra Mac Studio's memory options to only 96GB. Memory bandwidth reaches up to 1.2TB/s.

The M5 Ultra's media engine features twice the video encoding and decoding blocks of the M5 Max, supporting simultaneous processing of up to 33 streams of 8K ProRes video.

Apple shared the following M5 Ultra Mac Studio benchmark figures:

  • CopyCat ML training performance in Foundry Nuke is up to 15.4x faster than the Mac Studio with M1 Ultra, and up to 3.3x faster than M3 Ultra.
  • LLM prompt processing speed in LM Studio is up to 9.8x faster than the Mac Studio with M1 Ultra, and up to 4x faster than M3 Ultra.
  • Text-to-image performance is up to 8.2x faster than the Mac Studio with M1 Ultra, and up to 4.3x faster than M3 Ultra.
  • Scene rendering performance in Maxon Redshift is up to 4.7x faster than the Mac Studio with M1 Ultra, and up to 1.7x faster than M3 Ultra.

More Mac Studio specifications and details

  • Supports Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, powered by Apple's in-house N1 networking chip
  • Supports up to eight external displays, or up to four 5K-resolution Studio Display XDR at 120Hz refresh rate
  • Storage performance benefits from PCIe Gen 6 support, with speeds doubling
  • Thunderbolt 5, with bandwidth up to 120Gb/s
  • Supports genlock synchronization via USB-C, ensuring precise synchronization between displays and professional camera capture.

Mac Studio pricing and availability

The Mac Studio with M5 Max starts at $2,499, with the base configuration including 512GB of storage—same pricing as the M4 Max Mac Studio. The Mac Studio with M5 Ultra starts at $5,499 with 1TB of storage, representing a $200 increase over the M3 Ultra configuration.

Buy Mac Studio from Apple:

  • M5 Max Mac Studio: from $2,499 (education price $2,299)
  • M5 Ultra Mac Studio: from $5,499 (education price $5,099)

The new Mac Studio lineup is available for order starting today, with deliveries beginning September 22. However, Apple notes that the M5 Ultra Mac Studio configured with 512GB of memory will not be available until late October.
